title: To Thee, Great Source of Light
description: To Thee, Great Source of Light in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 156 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Perpetual Praise”, where the book credits them to the Sacred Lyrics.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To thee, great Source of light! My thank-ful voice I'll raise; And all my powers u-nite To cel-e-brate thy praise; And, till my voice is lost in death, May praise em-ploy my ev-ery breath.

lines: To thee, great Source of light!
And, till my voice is lost in death,
May praise employ my every breath.
Then, with the shining hosts above,
In nobler strains I'll sing thy love.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
